title: Compile nodes into instructions
description: You can follow how the compiler emits stack instructions and fills forward-jump targets.

steps.description: Instruction holds an opcode and optional operand. Chunk appends instructions and can patch an earlier operand.
The node classes describe the input tree. The compiler emits pushes for literals, loads for names, and a store after an assignment's value.
Ordinary binary operations compile both operands before their opcode. and and or instead emit jumps that can skip the right operand.

steps.question: When can the compiler replace the false-branch placeholder with its target?
steps.answer: After compiling the then-branch and its end jump, the next instruction position marks the else-branch start.

steps.description: The if case patches two forward targets. The while case records its condition position for a backward jump and patches its exit target.
Functions receive separate chunks. Calls compile the callee and arguments, while return and print emit their operations after compiling a value.
The demonstration prints compiled instructions rather than executing them. Its false jump and end jump both target instruction position 9 because the else-body is empty.
